statistics.duration: min(observed duration, 60 s), including every failure
statistics.bootstrap: 95% percentile, 5,000 resamples of paired seeds; equal episode weight
statistics.interval_scope: Pointwise descriptive intervals, not simultaneous multi-comparison claims
statistics.median: Median of observed times capped at 60 s; this is not an uncensored median time to failure
statistics.survival: Exact failure times; completed episodes right-censored only at the fixed 60 s endpoint

tracking.error: World-frame linear-velocity error norm ||v(t)-v_command(t)||, in m/s
tracking.rmse: sqrt(mean_t ||v(t)-v_command(t)||^2) within the explicitly recorded window
tracking.aggregate: Arithmetic mean of per-episode mean errors or per-episode RMSE; 95% intervals resample episode pairs
tracking.windows: matched_tracking_work.csv gives each [0,T) and its 500 Hz sample count; complete-pair windows have T=60 s
tracking.interpretation: Matched observed-state diagnostics, not an assigned post-fall error or the paper's incompletely defined Mean Cost

mechanical_work.torque: Saved torque is the clipped executed control passed to env.step; actual saved model has unit joint transmission and gain
mechanical_work.integration: Left rectangle using pre-step joint velocities and held executed torque for each 0.002 s step
mechanical_work.meaning: Estimate of positive actuator mechanical work; excludes electrical losses and is not battery energy
mechanical_work.complete_windows: Both-success pairs only, entire [0,60); conditional on both completing
mechanical_work.common_windows: Each matched pair uses [0,min(duration_fixed,duration_adaptive)); no zero-padding after a fall
mechanical_work.four_way_windows: four_group_common_prefix.csv; 50 seeds with the same prefix for all four groups
mechanical_work.aggregation: Mean of episode work and per-episode mean positive power; intervals resample episode pairs
mechanical_work.observed_columns: episodes.csv observed_* describe unequal observed durations and are not used as energy rankings

matched_identity: All 150 adaptive/fixed pairs have identical wrench schedules, executed common-prefix wrenches, commands and initial qpos/qvel; every trajectory hash verified

reference_downloads.contents: All 101 newly executed clock-corrected episodes, their actual runner/configuration files, and all 4 selected continuous videos. Original paths are retained.

fig3_resource_window.verdict: No competing GPU compute process or substantial external CPU workload observed in 35 snapshots. Normal desktop services remained active. This is an observed exclusive compute window, not a kernel hardware reservation.
fig3_resource_window.cpu_percent_definition: ps lifetime CPU percentage sampled every five seconds

historical_resource_blocker: On 2026-10-22 another training job occupied the GPU and CPU workers. It had ended by the 2026-10-23 resource-window check. The 3 deferred episodes were then run once; old shared timings were not reused.

baseline_selection.basis: Among the three tested fixed frequencies, 2.4 Hz has the highest observed 60 s completion (28/50) and capped mean duration (46.3486 s). Retain it as a strong fixed-frequency baseline in subsequent authorized comparisons.
baseline_selection.adaptive_comparison: Adaptive completes 22/50 and lasts 42.72 s on average. Adaptive-minus-fixed-2.4 paired duration is -3.6286 s, 95% interval [-10.250129,2.904257]; success difference is -12 percentage points, interval [-30,6]. Neither superiority nor equivalence between these two controllers is established.
baseline_selection.supported_adaptation_scope: Allowing frequency selection improves full-task outcomes relative to fixed 1.3 and fixed 2.0 Hz. These data do not establish that online selection is more robust than always using 2.4 Hz.
baseline_selection.work_tracking_tradeoff: On the 15 seeds where both adaptive and fixed 2.4 Hz complete 60 s, adaptive uses 1574.064 J less positive mechanical work on average (95% paired interval [-1927.053,-1158.756] J), while its velocity RMSE is 0.023942 m/s higher (interval [0.009092,0.042247]). This is a completion-conditioned mechanical-work comparison, not battery energy or an unconditional all-task efficiency claim.
baseline_selection.scope: Only 1.3, 2.0 and 2.4 Hz under this frozen task were compared. No claim of globally optimal frequency.
